titleStmt.title: Kephalaia of the Teacher, edition page 104: diplomatic and Leiden transcription

sourceDesc.bibl: Kephalaia (Manichäische Handschriften der Staatlichen Museen Berlin), ed. H. J. Polotsky and A. Böhlig, Stuttgart: Kohlhammer, 104. Restorations, sublinear dots, gap counts and corrections are the editors'.

encodingDesc.p: EpiDoc. Read by eye from the page image; gap counts, sublinear dots and supralinear stroke extents verified by measurement on the image. A supralinear stroke is marked on every letter it covers by at least half its width. Spaces are the edition's word division. Facsimile zones are measured line centres. The editors' German statements are not transcribed: each is mapped to an id of the controlled vocabulary data/kephalaia/editorial_vocabulary.json and carried as @ana (ed: statements in the text, app: apparatus footnotes, tr: categories of the transcriber's commentary).

"6 ⲡⲉ ⲡⲙⲟⲩ über der Zeile": the two words stand above the line in the manuscript; the place is named, so they are encoded `\ⲡⲉ ⲡⲙⲟⲩ/` (48.20).
"30 Lies ⲛⲟⲩⲱϣ": the correction adds ⲛ, encoded `⟨ⲛ⟩` (51.26).

div.p: The manuscript page number ⲣⲇ (top left, even page) with a bar above and below as the frame (no strokes). Running title [ⲛⲕⲉ]ⲫⲁⲗⲁⲓⲟⲛ with its first three letters restored in brackets, printed without ornaments and without a stroke over ⲛ. Every dot run was counted from the dot x-positions. Every ϣ on the page was checked on lower-zone sheets at 2.2× and the candidates at 8×: only 8 ⲃⲁϣⲟⲩ has a dot in the lower bowl; all have their tail. ⲯ in ⲙⲯ[ⲩⲭ]ⲁⲩⲉ (l. 7), ⲁϯⲯⲩⲭⲏ (l. 10) and ⲧⲟⲩⲑⲗⲓⲯⲓⲥ (l. 15): arms curving upwards and a stem through the baseline, against the straight ϯ of ϯⲛⲁϭ (l. 4) and the first letter of ⲁϯⲯⲩⲭⲏ (l. 10). Kephalaion 39 (opened 102.13) ends at l. 20 with "leer" and no end sign; kephalaion 40 opens at l. 21. Reconcile flags explained: l. 10 the ϩ dot joined to the letter (690); l. 14 the first seven bracket dots stand at the zone centre (530–662) and the foot of ⲁ of ⲛⲁϣⲱⲡⲉ is counted (882); l. 22 the feet of the left margin numeral (595, 603); l. 26 the feet of ⲙ of ⲙⲛⲧⲉϥ (951, 966); l. 28 the foot of ⲕ of ⲡⲉⲧⲁϥⲧⲱⲕ (1134). Spaces flags are dot runs, the legs of the enlarged Ⲡ (ll. 1, 6, 24, 31, 34), "leer" and the ornaments and margin numerals of the title lines.

Dots under ⲉ, ⲕ of ⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ (563, 577); dots under ⲙ, ⲛ of ⲙⲛ (877, 897) and a stroke over the ⲛ (893–905; ⲙ bare); stroke over ⲙ of ⲙⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ (1080–1093).
